findings.claim: Surah 46, verse 33 and surah 3, verse 16 are among the passages the spec highlights as scriptural anchors for this doctrine.
findings.truth: The specification pairs Qur'an 46:33 with 3:16 under Islamic beliefs about life after death in the thematic paper (Issues of Life and Death), not in the world-faith paper. The world-faith Islam option lists no ayah under Akhirah at all. The sentence also points students at 'the spec' in place of telling them what the verses say, and 3:16 is a believers' prayer for forgiveness and protection from the Fire, not a description of the afterlife.
findings.evidence: spec line 1202 (Component 1 Theme 2: 'Islamic beliefs and teachings about life after death, including soul, judgement, akhirah, heaven and hell: Qur'an 46:33, 3:16'); spec Islam option Akhirah rows carry no ayah; quran.com 3:16

findings.claim: the Qur'an (3:16) describes God's reward for those who are mindful of Him
findings.truth: 3:15 is the verse that describes the reward: gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, promised to those who are mindful of God. 3:16 is the prayer of the believers: 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' The answer key attributes 3:15's content to 3:16.

findings.claim: On arrival in Mecca, pilgrims enter a state of ritual purity (ihram), wearing two plain white sheets that remove all distinctions of wealth, nationality, and status.
findings.truth: Pilgrims enter ihram before they reach Mecca, at the boundary stations called miqat. The two unstitched white sheets (rida' and izar) are men's ihram dress; women wear ordinary plain, modest clothing and do not cover the face.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, 'Ihram' (entered before crossing the miqat; men's two white unhemmed sheets; women's dress varies and is not special clothing)

findings.claim: Pilgrims wear identical ihram garments, removing all distinctions of status
findings.truth: Ihram dress is not identical for all pilgrims: men wear two plain white sheets, women wear plain modest clothing. Same error as F3, repeated in the takeaway.

findings.claim: Plain white ihram garments, to remove all distinctions of wealth, nationality, and status before Allah.
findings.truth: The flashcard answer to 'What do pilgrims wear during Hajj and why?' should separate men's two white sheets from women's plain modest dress. Same error as F3, repeated in recall practice.

findings.claim: the events it re-enacts are rooted in the pre-Islamic history of Mecca
findings.truth: Muslims hold that Ibrahim submitted to the one God and dedicated the Ka'bah to him, so the Hajj's founding events are not 'pre-Islamic' in Muslim belief. In normal usage 'pre-Islamic Mecca' names the age of idol worship before Muhammad, which is the opposite of what the Hajj commemorates. Lesson 3 of this same unit teaches that Ibrahim rejected idol worship and rebuilt the Ka'bah for God alone.
findings.evidence: Qur'an 3:67 ('Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a Muslim'); L3 content_html of this unit

findings.claim: The 15-mark stems in L1 and L2 read 'Evaluate this statement, referring to Islamic teachings and non-religious perspectives.'
findings.truth: On the world-faith paper the spec says knowledge of non-religious traditions 'may be applied throughout the assessment of the specified content' - it is permitted, not demanded. The 15-mark task is to weigh more than one point of view with reference to religion and belief. Option A: reword both stems to ask for more than one point of view and keep non-religious material as optional in the mark scheme. Option B: leave them, since non-religious views are allowed and the schemes only offer them. L3's 15-mark stem already omits the clause, so the unit is inconsistent whichever way it goes. Recommend Option A.
findings.evidence: spec, Islam option preamble; spec 3.1 assessment objectives (Component 3: AO1 12.5% / AO2 12.5% of the qualification)
findings.ruling: Leave: relabel/build item or unverified iconography.

findings.claim: All three lessons label the 8-mark question '8 marks - Explain Two Beliefs' (three practice types plus three exam tips).
findings.truth: 'Explain two beliefs' is another board's printed question wording, used there at 4 and 5 marks. On this paper the 8-mark part is an explain task and answering it with two developed beliefs is sound advice, but it is not the question's form. Option A: relabel to '8 marks - Explain' in six places and move the two-belief advice into the tip text. Option B: keep the house label. Recommend Option A - the marks are right, only the borrowed name is wrong, and it repeats across every lesson.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1 AO grid (Component 3 splits 60 marks 30 AO1 / 30 AO2, consistent with 2+5+8 AO1 and 15 AO2 per question); spec gives no question wording
findings.ruling: Leave: relabel/build item or unverified iconography.

findings.claim: The three lessons teach Sunni Islam only.
findings.truth: The world-faith Islam option sets a large Shi'a strand: adalat, the five roots of Usul ad-Din, the Ten Obligatory Acts (salat, sawm, zakat and hajj plus amr-bil-maroof, nahi anil munkar, tawalla, tabarra, khums and jihad), khums, pilgrimage to Shi'a shrines and Ashura. It also sets Mika'il, Israfil, and attitudes to Kutub, Sahifah, Injil, Tawrat and Zabur. None of that appears in the unit, yet L1's third knowledge check uses Mika'il and Israfil as distractors for content never taught. Nothing present is misattributed, so this is a gap, not an error. Recommend a fourth lesson on Shi'a Islam rather than edits to these three.
findings.evidence: spec, Option 3 Islam: 'The six articles of faith in Sunni Islam / The five roots in Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam'; 'Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam'; 'Khums'; 'Ashura: The Day of Remembrance (Shi'a)'
findings.ruling: Leave: relabel/build item or unverified iconography.

findings.claim: the Most Merciful (Al-Rahman), the Most Compassionate (Al-Rahim)
findings.truth: The commoner pairing runs the other way: Al-Rahman the Most Gracious or Compassionate, Al-Rahim the Most Merciful. Both renderings appear in published translations and no marks turn on which is used.
findings.evidence: standard translations of the basmala (Sahih International 'the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful'; Clear Quran 'the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful')

findings.truth: The usual transliterations are sadaqah, du'a, and rak'ah for the singular with rak'at for the plural. Spelling, punctuation and grammar are not assessed on this paper and examiners accept variant transliterations, so no marks are at risk; worth tidying if the unit is ever rebuilt.
findings.evidence: standard GCSE Islam vocabulary lists; spec 3.1 ('SPaG is assessed in Components 1 and 2')

summary: Six fixes across lessons 2 and 3: the Hajj section put pilgrims into ihram on arrival in Mecca rather than at the miqat and dressed every pilgrim in the men's two white sheets (repeated in the takeaway and a flashcard), and called the Hajj's founding events 'pre-Islamic'; lesson 3 attributed a pair of afterlife ayat to the wrong paper of this qualification while pointing students at 'the spec', and its 8-mark answer key gave 3:15's content under 3:16. Every Qur'an citation, doctrine, date, name and answer key elsewhere checked out. Three items need Tom's ruling: the 15-mark stems that demand non-religious perspectives, the borrowed 'Explain Two Beliefs' label, and the missing Shi'a strand.
